Types of Musical Instruments of India

In Natya Shastra, Bharat Muni categorises Indian musical instruments into four main types: Avanaddha {membranophones}, Ghana {idiophones}, Sushira {aerophones} and Tat {chordophones}.

  1. 1. Tantu Vadya (Chordophones) → String Instruments
  • Sound is produced by plucking or bowing the stretched strings. E.g., Sitar, Sarod, Santoor, Veena, Rudra Veena, Violin, Surbahar, Guitar, Mohan Veena.
  1. 2. Sushir Vadya (Aerophones) → Wind Instruments
  • Sound is produced by blowing air through instrument. E.g., Flute, Shehnai, Nadaswaram.
  1. 3. Avanaddha Vadya (Membranophones) → Percussion Instruments
  • Sound is produced by striking a stretched membrane (made of animal skin) or drumhead. E.g., Tabla, Pakhawaj, Mridangam, Drums.

Percussion instruments are of two types:

  1. 1. Idiophones: An idiophone is any musical instrument that creates sound primarily by the vibration of the instrument itself, without the use of air flow, strings, membranes or electricity. E.g. Xylophones, bells, etc.
  2. 2. Membranophones: A membranophone is an instrument which produces sound by a stretched membrane that is struck or vibrated. E.g. Tabla, mridangam, etc.
  1. 4. Ghana Vadya (Idiophones) → Solid Instruments
  • Sound is produced by striking or shaking solid materials. E.g., Ghatam, Manjira, Kartal.

Some Traditional Instruments

  • Kamaicha: A bowed flute played by Manganairs of West Rajasthan.
  • Kartal: A wooden clapper from the state of Rajasthan that comes under Idiophones.
  • Chinkara: A stringed instrument played popularly in Madhya Pradesh.
  • Pena: A traditional stringed instrument that is played in states of Manipur and Assam.

Musical Instruments and Exponents

String Instruments (Tantu Vadya)

Sitar

  • Sitar is a plucked string instrument used in Hindustani music.
  • Exponents: Pt. Ravi Shankar
  • First Indian to win Grammy for the album "West Meets East" (1968).
  • He is also the Indian to win most no. of Grammys (a total of 5).
  • He is the second Indian musician to receive Bharat Ratna (India's highest civilian award) in 1999.
  • Anoushka Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Imrat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee, Budhaditya Mukherjee, Pt. Harashankar Bhattacharya, Arvind Parikh, Anupama Bhagwat, Rajeevea Janardhan (Imdadkhani Gharana).
  • First Grammy won by Mickey Hart in 1992.
  • First female to win Grammy: Tanvi Shah.
  • Father of Fusion dance (also known as "IIF" form of dance) → Pt. Uday Shankar (brother of Pt. Ravi Shankar).

Sarod

  • A stringed instrument known for its deep, resonant sound.
  • Exponents: Amjad Ali Khan
  • He is known as "Sarod Samrat".
  • He is known for fast and clear ektara taan.
  • He has received Padma Bhushan (1991) and Padma Vibhushan (2001).
  • Alauddin Khan (Maihar Gharana), Ali Akbar Khan (Maihar Gharana), Hafiz Ali Khan, Rajeev Taranath (disciple of Ali Akbar Khan), Buddhadev Dasgupta.

Santoor

  • It is known as "Shattantri Veena" in Sanskrit and has 72 strings.
  • Exponents: Shivkumar Sharma
  • He popularised Santoor.
  • He has received Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1986) and Padma Vibhushan (2001).
  • Rahul Sharma, Ulhas Bapat, Bhajan Sapori, Tarun Bhattacharya (won Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018), Hafiz Ali Khan (Padma Vibhushan in 1998).

Sarangi

  • It is a bowed, short-necked instrument often used in classical and folk music.
  • Exponents: Pt. Ram Narayan (Padma Vibhushan in 2005), Ustad Sabri Khan, Bundu Khan, Binda Khan, Shakoor Khan, Abdul Latif Khan, Ustad Sultan Khan.

Veena

  • It is an ancient, revered stringed instrument.
  • Samudragupta (Gupta Dynasty) is depicted playing Veena on his coins.
  • Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb and former PM APJ Abdul Kalam also played Veena.
  • Exponents: S. Balachander, Jayanthi Kumaresh (plays Saraswati Veena), Chitti Babu, E. Sankara Sastry, Doraiswamy Iyengar.
  • Saraswati Veena is crafted from the wood of Jackfruit.

String Instruments (continued)

Rudraveena

  • It is used in Dhrupad music.
  • Exponents: Asad Ali Khan, Zia Mohiuddin Dagar, Sadik Ali Khan.

Surbahar

  • It is a plucked string instrument also known as bass sitar.
  • Exponents: Annapurna Devi, Ustad Imrat Khan (also known as Surbahar instrument master), Wahid Khan, Imdad Khan.

Violin

  • It is a stringed instrument with 4 strings held against the shoulder under the chin and played with a bow.
  • Exponents: T.N. Krishnan (Padma Bhushan in 1992), Nagai Muralidharan, Lalgudi Gopala Iyer Jayaraman (Padma Bhushan in 2001), Mohanan Chandrasekaran (an awardee of Madras Music Academy's Kalanidhi), Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu, V.G. Jog, N. Rajam, Ragini Shankar, Nandini Shankar, M. Gopalkrishna (Padma Bhushan in 2012), Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan, Lakshminarayana Subramam, Mysore Nagaraj and Mysore Manjunath (Mysore Brothers).

Mandolin

  • A mandolin is a stringed musical instrument in the lute family and is generally plucked with a pick.
  • Exponents: U. Srinivas, S Balamuralikrishna, Nagen Dey, Khagen Dey.

Guitar

  • It is a stringed instrument with 6 strings that is played by plucking or strumming.
  • Exponents: Brij Bhushan Kabra (won Sangeet Natak Academy in 2005), Thakur Chakrapani Singh.

Mohan Veena

  • It is a modified Hawaiian guitar with 20 strings.
  • Exponents: Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt
  • He won Grammy (1994) for album "A Meeting by the River".
  • He also won Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1998) and Padma Bhushan (2017).

Ektara

  • Ektara is a single string, musical instrument made using bamboo and a gourd, mostly used by traditional folk singers in Maharashtra.

Wind Instruments (Sushir Vadya)

Flute (Bansuri)

  • It is a wind instrument consisting of a tube and 6 or 7 fingerholes.
  • Exponents: Hariprasad Chaurasiya
  • He was born in Prayagraj.
  • He has received Padma Bhushan (1992) and Padma Vibhushan (2000).
  • Pannalal Ghosh (other name: Amal Jyoti Ghosh), Rajendra Prasanna, Rajendra Kulkarni, Rakesh Chaurasiya, Prabhat Sharma.
  • Prasanna surname associated with Flute.

Shehnai

  • It is an instrument made of wood that has 7 fingerholes.
  • It is also known as Mangala Vadya (auspicious instrument).
  • Exponents: Ustad Bismillah Khan
  • He was born in Dumraon, Bihar.
  • He played Shehnai at Red Fort on India's first Independence Day (15th August 1947).
  • He has received all the four highest civilian awards: Bharat Ratna (2001), Padma Vibhushan (1980), Padma Bhushan (1968) and Padma Shri (1961).
  • The Iranian city of Tehran named an auditorium after him → Tahar Mosiquee Ustaad Bismillah Khan.
  • He is also the 3rd Indian musician to receive Bharat Ratna.
  • Raghunath Prasanna (also plays flute), S. Ballesh, Ali Ahmed, Bageswari Quamar, Krishna Chaudhary.

Nadaswaram

  • It is similar to Shehnai but larger in size, mostly played in South Indian temples.
  • Exponents: T.N. Rajarathinam Pillai, Rajratna Pillai, Neeru Swami Pillai, Sheikh Chinna Maulana.

Harmonium

  • A harmonium is a keyboard instrument that produces sound by blowing air through metal reeds.
  • Exponent: Tulsidas Borkar.
  • "Aur yeh toh pata hi hoga ki abba humare Harmonium bajate the".

Percussion Instruments (Avanaddha Vadya)

Tabla

  • Exponents: Zakir Hussain
  • Total Grammy received: 4
  • He has received a total of 3 Grammy (in 2024) for: "Pashto", "As We Speak", "This Moment" with fusion music group Shakti.
  • 4th Grammy for a collaborative album "Global Drum Project".
  • He has received Padma Bhushan (2002) and Padma Vibhushan (2023).
  • Nikhil Ghosh (Padma Bhushan in 1990), Bickram Ghosh, Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay (Benaras Gharana), Anokhelal Mishra, Pt. Swapan Choudhary, Ananda Gopal Bandopadhyay, Shubhankar Banerjee, Shreya Bhattacharjee.

Pakhawaj

  • It is used in Dhrupad music.
  • Exponents: Kunal Patil, Tota Ram Sharma, Pt. Bhavani Shankar, Ustad Rahman Khan, Kelucharan Mohapatra.
  • Pudukkotai Dakshinamurthi Pillai is renowned for his exceptional skills in playing the Kanjira.

Mridangam

  • A mridangam is a double-headed drum used in South Indian classical music.
  • Exponents: Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman
  • He has received Padma Bhushan (2003), Padma Vibhushan (2010), and Sangeet Natak Akademi (1992).
  • V.K. Sivaraman, Rajna Swaminathan, Guruvayur Dorai, RV Raghavan.

Ghatam

  • It is a clay pot used as a percussion instrument.
  • Exponents: E. M. Subramaniyam
  • He was awarded the title of "Kalaimamani" (2000) and has won Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2011).

TH Vinaykram

  • He is also known as Vikku Vinaykram.
  • He has received Padma Bhushan (2014).

Drums

  • Drums make sound when struck.
  • Exponents: Sivamani.

Key concepts

  • Tantu Vadya (String) – Sitar, Sarod, Veena, Violin
  • Sushir Vadya (Wind) – Flute, Shehnai, Nadaswaram, Harmonium
  • Avanaddha Vadya (Percussion) – Tabla, Pakhawaj, Mridangam, Ghatam, Drums
  • Ghana Vadya (Solid/Idiophones) – Ghatam, Manjira, Kartal
  • Pt. Ravi Shankar – 5 Grammys, Bharat Ratna 1999
  • Ustad Bismillah Khan – Shehnai maestro, Bharat Ratna 2001, played at Red Fort 1947
  • Zakir Hussain – 4 Grammys, Padma Vibhushan 2023

Factual Verifications

  • Natya Shastra four-fold classification (Avanaddha, Ghana, Sushira, Tat) by Bharat Muni — confirmed.
  • Pt. Ravi Shankar: 5 Grammys, Bharat Ratna 1999 — verified. "West Meets East" (1968) was indeed his first Grammy-winning album. "Father of Fusion dance" attributed to Uday Shankar (his brother) — verified.
  • Ustad Bismillah Khan: All 4 Padma awards (Padma Shri 1961, Padma Bhushan 1968, Padma Vibhushan 1980, Bharat Ratna 2001), born Dumraon Bihar, played Shehnai at Red Fort on 15 Aug 1947 — verified.
  • Zakir Hussain: Padma Bhushan 2002, Padma Vibhushan 2023; recent Grammy wins (4 total) for fusion work with Shakti and "Global Drum Project" — verified.
  • Shivkumar Sharma: Sangeet Natak Akademi 1986, Padma Vibhushan 2001, popularised Santoor — verified.
  • Amjad Ali Khan: "Sarod Samrat," Padma Bhushan 1991, Padma Vibhushan 2001 — verified.
  • Pt. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt: Grammy 1994 for "A Meeting by the River," Padma Bhushan 2017, Sangeet Natak Akademi 1998 — verified.
  • Hariprasad Chaurasiya: Padma Bhushan 1992, Padma Vibhushan 2000 — verified.
  • Santoor: 72 strings, called "Shattantri Veena" — verified.
  • Veena: Samudragupta coins, APJ Abdul Kalam as veena player — verified.
  • Hafiz Ali Khan Padma Vibhushan 1998 — verified.
